BiblicalUsage: Zarab pictures a desert stream that runs in the rainy season and dries to nothing in the heat. Job reaches for it when his friends fail him: they were like a brook that promises water and then vanishes when he comes thirsty to drink.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe fair-weather friends are worse than no friends at all, because they raise hope and then leave you dry.
